To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MTHFD1 and MTHFR C667T polymorphisms are associated with antipsychotic treatment-induced changes in metabolic parameters in schizophrenia patients.

the MTHFD1 1958A allele carriers had higher total cholesterol, low density lipoprotein, triglyceride, and homocysteins levels, while the MTHFD 1958GG genotype had lower total cholesterol, low and high density loprotein, and triglyceride levels, compared to other corresponding genotypes.

the MTHFD1 1958AA genotype and MTHFR 1298CC genotype were associated with lower levels of homocysteines, and that the MTHFC 677CC genotype was associated with a higher increase in body weight and waist circumference during 12 weeks treatment with second-generation anti-psychotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the MTHFD1 G1958A, MTRR A66G, and BHMT G742A polymorphisms in the development of metabolic parameters in first-episode patients during the first 12 weeks of exposure to antipsyhotic treatment.
the role of genetic variation in one-carbon metabolism and its effect on metabolic parameters during treatment with second-generation anti-psychotics in firstepisode schizophrenia patients.
the role of genetic variation in 1-carbin metabolism in antipsychotic-associated changes in metabolic parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MTHFD1 1958G>A, MTHFR 1298A>C, and MTHFR 667C>T polymorphisms may predict antipsycotic induced weight gain and waist circumference, and the MTRR A66G and BHMT 742G>A polymorphisms do not have such effects.
the MTHFD1, MTRR, and BHMT polymorphisms do not predict antipsychotics-induced changes in metabolic parameters.
the MTHFD1 G1958A polymorphism might have a protective effect on the development of metabolic syndrome in patients with schizophrenia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MTHFD1 1958A, MTHFR 1298A, and MTRR 66G alleles were associated with higher homocysteines and lower folates.
the MTHFD1 1958AA and MTHFR 1298AA genotypes and the MTRR 66GG and BHMT 742AA genotypes may protect patients against antipsychotic-related weight gain.
the MTHFD1 and MTHFR polymorphisms may be involved in antipsychotic-associated weight gain and the MTHFR and BHMT polymorphisms may affect antipsychotic-related changes in lipid profiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MTHFR polymorphism might predict weight gain during initial exposure to antypsychotic treatment.
genetic variation in one-carbon metabolism genes might be a useful tool to predict antipsychotics-induced weight gain in first-episode patients.
genetic polymorphisms in folate metabolism genes might be used as predictors of antipsychotic-related metabolic side effects.
